Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 88, verse 1–3:

Surah al-Ghashiyah is Meccan. [[Al-Suyuti cites Ibn al-Daris, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "Surat al-Ghashiyah was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh also narrates the same from al-Zubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8 / 490.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Has the news of the Overwhelming (al-Ghashiyah) reached you?﴾ That is: the news of the Resurrection has indeed reached you, which overwhelms everything with its terrors.

﴿Faces on that Day﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will be humbled﴾, abased.

﴿Labouring, weary﴾. 'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means those who labored and toiled in this world, not upon the religion of Islam, from among the worshippers of idols and disbelieving People of the Book, such as the monks and others. Allah does not accept from them the striving in error; they will enter the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. This is the statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam. The meaning of nasab (toil) is persistent exertion in labor with fatigue.

'Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: laboring in this world in sins, and weary in the Hereafter in the Fire. [[Al-Suyuti attributes this in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8 / 491 to Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Some of them said: laboring in the Fire and weary therein. Al-Hasan said: they did not work for Allah in this world, so He makes them labor and weary in the Fire, by being treated with chains and shackles. Qatadah said likewise, and it is a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. [[See: al-Tabari: 30 / 160.]]

Ibn Mas'ud said: they will wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

al-Kalbi said: they will be dragged upon their faces in the Fire.

[Al-Dahhak said: they will be commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire.] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] The speech is framed in terms of "faces," and what is meant is their owners.

﴿They will enter a fire﴾. The people of Basra and Abu Bakr recited "tuṣlā" (with a dammah on the tā'), by analogy with His words "they will be given to drink from a boiling spring" [the others recited it with a fathah on the tā'] ﴿a scorching fire﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it has been heated, and so it blazes against the enemies of Allah.

﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring﴾, extremely hot. Jahannam has been kindled over it since it was created, and they are driven to it [wirdan] [[In manuscript A: "wardū" (they came to the water).]] thirsty. The exegetes (mufassirun) said: if one drop from it fell upon the mountains of the world, they would melt. This is their drink. Then He mentioned their food, saying: ﴿They will have no food except from ḍarī'﴾. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which Quraysh call al-shibraq; when it grows dry they call it al-ḍarī'. It is the most loathsome and repulsive food. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries out.

Ibn Zayd said: as for in this world, al-ḍarī' is the dry thorn whose leaves have withered; but in the Hereafter it is a thorn of fire [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/161-162.]]. And there came in a hadith from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-ḍarī' is something in the Fire, resembling a thorn [shibh] [[In manuscript B: yushbih.]], more bitter than aloes, more foul-smelling than carrion, and hotter than the Fire" [[Cited by the author of al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/492-493 from Ibn Mardawayh, with a very weak chain.]].

Then they call for help again and are given food that chokes. They remember that in the world they used to ease choking with water, so they ask for water, and they are given thirst for a thousand years. Then they are given to drink from a boiling spring a drink that is neither wholesome nor pleasant. When they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them to pieces. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: "And they are given boiling water to drink, which cuts their bowels to pieces" [Muhammad: 15] [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/492 from Ibn Mardawayh.]].

The commentators (al-Mufassirun) said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said, "Indeed our camels grow fat on *al-dari'* (ضَرِيع)!" They were lying in this, for camels only graze on it while it is fresh and green, and it is called "*shabraq*" (شَبْرَق). When it dries out, nothing eats it. So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger﴾.

Then He described the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾. Muqatil said: "In blessing and honour."

﴿Pleased with their striving﴾ in the worldly life, ﴿well-pleased﴾ in the Hereafter, when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds.

﴿In a lofty garden, where they will hear no idle talk﴾: *laghw* (لَغْوٌ), meaning vain and false speech. The people of Makkah and Basra recited "*la yusma'u*" (لَا يُسْمَعُ) with a *ya'* and a *damma*, and "*laghiyatun*" (لَاغِيَةٌ) in the nominative. Nafi' recited "*la tusma'u*" (لَا تُسْمَعُ) with a *ta'* and a *damma*, and "*laghiyatun*" in the nominative. The others recited with a *ta'* and a *fatha*, "*laghiyatan*" (لَاغِيَةً) in the accusative, addressing the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿Therein is a flowing spring, therein are couches raised high﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Their frames are of gold, inlaid with chrysolite, pearls and rubies, raised high. When its occupant does not come, they remain high; but when he wishes to sit upon them, they lower themselves for him until he sits, and then they rise back to their places.

﴿And cups set in place﴾ before them, the plural of *kub* (كُوبٌ), which is a *ibriq* (إبريق, a pitcher) that has no handle.

﴿And cushions﴾, meaning pillows and armrests, ﴿arranged in rows﴾, some beside others. Its singular is "*numruqah*" (نُمْرُقَةٌ) with a *damma* on the *nun*.

﴿And carpets﴾, meaning the wide rugs. Ibn 'Abbas said: They are the *tanafis* (طَنَافِس, thick woven coverings) that have nap, the singular of which is "*zarbiyyah*" (زَرْبِيَّةٌ). ﴿Spread out﴾, meaning laid out; and it was said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ The commentators said: When Allah, exalted is He, described in this surah what is in Paradise, the disbelievers marvelled at it and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His handiwork and said: ﴿Do they not look at the camels﴾ [among all other animals] ﴿how they were created?﴾ The camels were among the livelihood of the Arabs, and they had many benefits from them. Since He made that for them in this world, He made for the people of Paradise in it what He made.

The wise men (al-Hukama') discussed the reason for singling out the camel from among all other animals. Muqatil said: Because they had never seen a beast larger than it, and few of them had seen an elephant.

Al-Kalbi said: Because it rises with its load while kneeling.

Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the height of the couches and carpets of Paradise, so they said, "How will we climb them?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant more wondrous?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from knowing it. Moreover, it has no good in it: its back is not ridden, its meat is not eaten, and its milk is not milked. The camel is the most precious and valuable property of the Arabs; it eats date stones and fodder, and it produces milk.

It was also said: Despite its size, it yields to a heavy load and submits to a weak handler, to the extent that a small child takes hold of its halter and leads it wherever he wishes. Shurayh the judge used to say: "Come with us to the dung heap of the stable, so that we may look at the camels, how they were created." [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/165.]

Moreover, it has no good in it: its back is not ridden, its meat is not eaten, and its milk is not milked. The camel is the most precious and valuable property of the Arabs; it eats date stones and fodder, and it produces milk.

It was also said: Despite its size, it yields to a heavy load and submits to a weak handler, to the extent that a small child takes hold of its halter and leads it wherever he wishes. Shurayh the judge used to say: "Come with us to the dung heap of the stable, so that we may look at the camels, how they were created." [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/165.]

The commentators (al-Mufassirun) said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said, "Indeed our camels grow fat on *al-dari'* (ضَرِيع)!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger﴾.

Then He described the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾. Muqatil said: "In blessing and honour."

﴿Pleased with their striving﴾ in the worldly life, ﴿well-pleased﴾ in the Hereafter, when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds.

﴿In a lofty garden, where they will hear no idle talk﴾: *laghw* (لَغْوٌ), meaning vain and false speech. Nafi' recited "*la tusma'u*" (لَا تُسْمَعُ) with a *ta'* and a *damma*, and "*laghiyatun*" in the nominative. The others recited with a *ta'* and a *fatha*, "*laghiyatan*" (لَاغِيَةً) in the accusative, addressing the Prophet ﷺ.
